text.p: Nickel ended sharply lower and other metals were softer on the London Metals Exchange, while wheat closed mixed and crude gained on a strike threat and short covering. The Commodity Research Bureau index closed up 1.55 at 241.61.
Nickel briefly touched a fresh nine-month buying during early trade but failed to sustain its upward move and fell sharply by the close. The metal ended well down at $7,850.
Copper action was subdued early and prices struggled to $2,375 before falling back to end lower at $2,350. The cash/threes were narrower.
In the short term, the market could well be restrained by resistance between $2,385 and $2,400, with backwardations not causing any concern, traders added.
Aluminium also gained in early trade to a new nine month buying high before ending softer at $1,651.
Zinc pushed upwards early, buttressed by a 1,400-tonne stock fall, and closed easier as prices moved back to $1,200. Lead was dull again, and edged lower, while tin and alloy were equally quiet.
Tin ended just above $5,900, and alloy was weaker with the primary.

WHEAT CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby contracts higher on speculative short covering tied to a fund-related rally in soybeans, traders said. Volume in wheat was muted and the market was pressured by a Sparks Companies estimate for 1997 U.S. wheat production at 2.44 billion bushels, above a USDA outlook for 2.27 billion bushels, traders said. Wheat closed 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 5-1/2 lower, with March up two at $3.77.

NYMEX crude rebounded as a threats by petroleum industry workers in Nigeria to go on strike helped drive short covering throughout the oil complex after Monday's sharp decline, traders said. April crude settled up 29 cents at $21.00 a barrel, after rising as high as $21.31.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures prices were mainly higher on light volumes, as the market continued to digest last week's sharp gains. COMEX April gold closed up 90 cents at $356.10 an ounce, but was still below last Friday's 18-day high at $356.80.
